question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $5,$ denoted ${3}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
3\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(3,5)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $5.$

Since the modulus $n=5$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $3$ (modulo $5$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & ≡3\cdot 3≡9≡5+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ {3}^{3} & ≡3\cdot 4≡12≡2\cdot 5+2≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ {3}^{4} & ≡3\cdot 2≡6≡5+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $3\cdot 2≡1\,(\text{mod}\,5).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $5$ is $2.$
